title: Runner: a seeded nested item cap, and per-run manifests
description:
Spec first (specs beside the module), then code. The collectors take the amendment's rule: order each cell's items by the seeded hash and answer only the first N (cap 500 items), keeping originals with twins. Existing answer files stay valid; a later larger cap only requests the new items (resumable).

Also generate one manifest per run under docs/kev-runs/<task>.json (same schema and pinned hashes as docs/kev-coverage-first-slice.json, holding only the still-missing cells of that task), and the same for Jev under docs/jev-runs/. `bd replay` must still reproduce studies/ byte for byte.

Depends on the amendment task. Done when a dry run of every manifest reports the capped request counts.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Done in d3bac5c. biased_decisions/subsample.py (registered ranking, family = source_id/counterfactual_of, task prefix stripped) with 9 specs; collect(item_cap=) plans and answers only the sample and its record covers exactly those inputs (4 new specs); manifests carry item_cap per cell and validate against the capped count; make_kev_manifest --runs-dir writes one manifest per task for the cells a model lacks. Generated docs/kev-runs/*.json for Kev: 8 runs, 70,477 requests, every one passes run_kev_study dry-run. Limits: growing a sample later needs a step that seeds a larger run from a smaller record (a capped record is not reused for the full cell; a spec pins that). Jev runs are NOT generated: scripts/collect_task.py only supports Kev, so how Jev is collected needs looking at first.
